items.remaining: The route still offers no edit, rename or delete of a target.

batches.family: F03/F05: the shared clause library validates what it stores, reserves public publishing to an officer, and writes only rows it owns

items.explanation: Clause create, update and sharing bodies pass a zod schema before anything is stored: text, titles and names are bounded, dates are real calendar days, province is a 2-letter code, ids are ids, sharing levels are the four known ones, grants are at most 200 ids, and unknown fields are dropped. A malformed body is a 400. Existing route tests were adapted: organization and agreement fixtures that were not ids became ids, and handler calls that publish publicly carry an officer role (disclosed).
items.remaining: The tag write route still reads its body without the schema.

items.explanation: Setting a clause to public sharing on create, update or the share route now requires an officer role; a steward, a member or an unresolved role is refused with 403 before any read or write. Narrower scopes stay with the owning steward and keep their federation and congress eligibility checks.
items.remaining: The floor is a role title; no mandate-kernel decision names who may publish collective-agreement text.

items.explanation: A cited originalClauseId must be a clause of a collective agreement of the caller own organization (joined through the agreement); a missing or foreign one is a 404 and nothing is inserted. The id must also be well-formed.

A comparison no longer increments comparisonCount on rows another organization owns: it is a read of those rows and writes only the usage counter of the caller own clauses. The audit stays with the comparing organization.

batches.family: F12: an ICRA assessment exists only with server-stamped consent and is scored only from the required answers

items.explanation: The one-shot submit builds the stored consent on the server from the three acknowledgements (time and doctrine version stamped here; client time, version and extra keys dropped), accepts only the en-CA and fr-CA locales, reads the body as text under a 64 KB cap (413 beyond), and refuses organization-context keys that are not short lower-case identifiers or exceed 40. Unit and source-contract tests added; existing route tests still pass.

The stepwise flow requires all three acknowledgements to start (400 otherwise, consent stamped by the server), the answer route refuses to store anything for an assessment with no recorded consent (409), and so does the stepwise submit. No application caller of these routes existed. Existing tests were adapted: assessment fixtures now carry a recorded consent, the start 500 test sends consent, and the submit tests mock the coverage helper (disclosed); new tests cover the refusals.

The stepwise submit scores nothing unless every question the routing engine requires for an unclassified organization has an answer (400 with the missing count otherwise), using the same routed-submission validator as the live flow. Proven against the real question bank: one answer is refused, a full set is accepted.

batches.family: F12: cognition and knowledge-transfer results do not present absence, defaults or literals as measurement

items.explanation: The documentation strategy is selected when the documentation score is low (under 65) or unmeasured (missing or not finite), and not for any high score. The expression that parsed as score ?? (0 < 65) is gone. Source-contract test added.
The precedence defect in the documentation rule is corrected (same fix as the companion defect).
items.remaining: The projected resilience, governance and dependency gains of each strategy are still literal numbers from a per-strategy table.

items.explanation: With fewer than two entries and sessions the profiler now returns a new insufficient_data type with no characteristics and an identity statement that says so, instead of Resilience-Fragile. The existing no-history test pinned the old label and was changed to assert the new behaviour (disclosed).

Every derived analysis that read all published exit interviews now reads at most 500, newest as the database returns them, through one shared constant, so the work and the model prompt no longer grow without bound. Six test mocks gained a limit step on the query chain (disclosed; behaviour unchanged).
items.remaining: The 500 are not ordered by recency, and the topic graph still builds a pair edge for every two tags of each interview.

items.explanation: A narrative whose envelope carries no evidence now says that no institutional evidence is attached and that the result is guidance, not a finding, instead of "Derived from 0 institutional evidence items".
items.remaining: The headline is still the first sentence of fixed interpretation guidance and the engines still emit no evidence, reasoning or implications.

items.explanation: Existing implementation, verified: the resilience index refuses an organization with no dependency data with a conflict instead of computing NaN scores, so no strong status or brief is derived from it; an existing test covers both the empty and the interviews-without-nodes cases.

batches.family: F05/F12: searches match literally and list only active organizations; free-form JSON from callers is bounded and cannot overwrite audited fields

items.explanation: The organization search always excludes the platform organization type and any organization whose status is not active (a missing status counts as active), with or without a term, matches the term literally (percent and underscore escaped), and orders by name then id. The real-SQL pglite test for the search still passes, and a source-contract test pins the predicates.

The onboarding event payload bounds targetUserId (255) and role (64), limits metadata to 20 keys of short scalar values, and stores caller metadata before targetUserId and role so it can never replace the values the audit row records.
items.remaining: The event is still a caller-asserted milestone (tracked by the companion defect).

items.explanation: The anonymous pilot application bounds responses to 16 KB, 60 keys and 4 levels of nesting, and keeps only a finite numeric or short string assessment score instead of a passthrough object. Unit tests cover each bound.
items.remaining: The stored responses are still free-form JSON that later reads, proposals and exports consume; no per-key schema exists.

batches.family: F06: regulatory records and integration sync history are not erased by the generic delete

items.explanation: New crud-factory option retainOnDelete: DELETE answers 409 before any lookup or write, so the row is kept. Applied to the anti-scab violation and joint health-and-safety committee item routes, the two tables the defect names. A contract test pins that the refusal comes before any audited write or tx.delete.
The right-of-refusal item route declares retainOnDelete, so the refusal record and any reprisal complaint are never removed through the generic delete (409).
items.remaining: No retention rule is named by a source, so the record is retained rather than archived; a governed withdrawal action is still to be defined.

items.explanation: Deleting an integration first confirms it belongs to the organization (404 otherwise), then refuses with 409 when any synchronization history exists, so the cascade can never erase it; the integration is disabled instead. The existing extensions test was adapted to the new query sequence and gained the history case (disclosed).

batches.family: F05/F03: the social export is a bounded staff read with safe cells; records are looked up inside the caller organization

items.explanation: The export is now a steward-floor read with its own rate limit, at most 5000 rows per dataset, CSV cells neutralised through the shared formula-safe helper, zero values no longer blanked, and the campaign export reads each column by its real key (it previously left most columns empty). Existing analytics route tests still pass; a source-contract test pins each point.
items.remaining: It is still served on the DELETE verb, and no audit record is written for the export.

items.explanation: The post delete and the campaign analytics lookups name the caller organization inside the query (the post through an inner join to its account), so another organization row is simply not found (404) and the 403-versus-404 existence oracle is gone. The campaign routes already did this. The post delete test mock gained the inner join and now expects 404 for a foreign post (disclosed).

batches.family: F08: stored credentials and access configuration fail closed

items.explanation: The SSO provider create now accepts only saml or oidc, bounds every text field, requires https URLs without credentials for the SSO URL and issuer, requires the fields of the type when the provider is to be enabled, and creates a provider disabled and without auto-provisioning unless the administrator asks otherwise. The existing route tests pass unchanged; new unit tests cover each rule.
items.remaining: No unique index on organization, entity id or issuer, no proof the organization owns the identity domain, and requireGroups still cannot be set.

items.explanation: A provider token is never stored without an encryption key (development included; plaintext only under the test runner), and a stored value with no encryption prefix is refused unless CALENDAR_TOKEN_ALLOW_LEGACY_PLAINTEXT is set for a flagged migration window. New unit tests cover round trip, missing key in development and production, and the legacy flag.
items.remaining: Existing plaintext rows need a one-time re-encryption or re-authorization; none is performed here.

items.explanation: The entitlement list now names only the feature keys that the server-side checkModuleEntitlement allows (not expired, backing contract active) and is limited to 200 rows. Contract test pins the check.

batches.family: F03: an id taken from a body must name a row of the caller organization

items.explanation: The training session create checks that the course is the organization own (shared reference helper, 404 otherwise) and accepts only an allow-list of descriptive fields: registration, waitlist, attendance, completion, rating, evaluation, cost, status and cancellation figures are no longer body-writable. Contract test pins the allow-list and the check.

Logging an employer communication checks employerId, grievanceId, recipientContactId and templateId against the caller organization before any write (404, nothing written or audited), and the list is limited to 200. The existing route test mock gained the limit step and a new test covers a foreign grievance (disclosed).

batches.family: F12: routes that record a send or advertise an operation they do not perform answer 501; communications history is retained

items.explanation: The SMS message, campaign and conversation collections keep their officer-floor read, and their POST (which inserted rows carrying status, provider id, price and delivery times for messages never sent) now answers 501 and writes nothing. Contract test pins the read and the refusal.

The conversation read path no longer lists every message of the organization or inserts a message row: both methods answer 501 at the officer floor. The F07 read-authority contract test listed this path among the CRUD floors and was adjusted to drop it (disclosed); the new test pins the 501.
Both message-template item routes declare retainOnDelete: DELETE answers 409 and the template (and the campaign links it keeps) survives.
items.remaining: No archive or withdrawal action exists yet, so a template can no longer be removed through the API.

items.explanation: The distribution-list item route declares retainOnDelete, so a delete can no longer cascade away the subscribed, unsubscribed and unsubscribe-reason history of the list.
items.remaining: No archive action exists yet.

items.explanation: A job id that is not a campaign job, or a campaign of another organization, is answered 404 instead of a fabricated processing status with a start time of now; the failed-recipient list names a recipient id, not an e-mail address.
Existing implementation, verified by a new source-contract test: both filing paths answer 501 and neither is the generic campaign CRUD any more.
Existing implementation, verified: the form generation path answers 501 and no longer inserts or lists campaign rows.
items.remaining: The client still saves a JSON response as a PDF; the form generator itself is not built.

items.explanation: Existing implementation, verified: the bookings path answers 501 for GET and POST, reads and writes no room or booking row.
items.remaining: The room_bookings table is not migrated; the booking rules in lib/services/room-booking-rules.ts are not wired in.

items.explanation: Existing implementation, verified: the carbon dashboard no longer reads an organization id from the query string and no longer returns figures; it answers 501.

Existing implementation, verified: the response create verifies the survey belongs to the caller organization, is active and open, and strips respondent identity for an anonymous survey; the list is a count-only steward read of the path survey.
items.remaining: The POST still takes the survey id from the body rather than the path.

batches.family: F12: referenced ids belong to the right parent, and a figure with nothing to measure is unknown rather than 0 or 100

items.explanation: Target health now reads its direction from the thresholds: critical above warning above target means lower is better, and the comparison flips; otherwise higher is better as before. A missing or non-finite value or target is no_data. Pure unit tests cover both directions.
items.remaining: The direction is inferred from threshold order because no direction column exists; a column is the proper fix. The current value is still the latest row of the metric type.

items.explanation: relatedProposalIds are now an array of at most 50 ids, each of which must be a proposal of the same negotiation, and relatedClauseId must be a clause of an agreement of the caller organization (404 otherwise, nothing written). Existing route tests pass.
The filings collection sets staffReadsAll, so the member-id owner scope applies only below the steward floor and a steward reads the organization filings, as the item routes already allow.

Deadline adherence and documentation rate are null, not 100, when there is nothing to measure, and the card shows a dash in a neutral colour. The empty-input service test pinned the 100 and was changed to expect null (disclosed).
items.remaining: No code inserts compliance alerts, and the grievance aggregates still stop at the first 5000 rows.

items.explanation: The inspection findings list reports a missing score as null (shown as a dash) instead of 0%. The statistics and dashboard routes already reported unmeasured values as null (existing implementation, existing tests pass).
Adding a primary contact demotes the employer previous primary contact in the same transaction, so at most one is primary per create.
items.remaining: No unique index enforces it, so two concurrent creates could still both be primary.

items.explanation: Existing implementation, verified by a new test: neither collection declares an owner column the table lacks, so no declared-but-unapplied owner condition remains.
Existing implementation, verified by a new test: event create checks the calendar belongs to the caller organization and is not another member personal calendar (404).
items.remaining: The event update route does not re-check a changed calendarId.

batches.family: F12: approved records are locked, reviewers are independent, referenced members and documents are the organization own, and an unsubscribe is one transaction

items.explanation: A meeting update that touches decisions, agenda items, agenda or status is conditional on the minutes not yet being approved; when they are, the update answers 409 (404 only for a missing meeting). Other fields (location, link) stay editable. Existing committee tests pass; a source-contract test pins the predicate.
The person who last edited the meeting record, which includes recording the minutes, cannot approve them (403).
items.remaining: The table records no separate recorder, so the last editor stands in for the recorder; a recordedBy column is the proper fix.

items.explanation: Attendance member ids and an action-item assignee must be current members of the organization (400, nothing written), and a linked documentId must be a document of the organization (404). Existing committee tests pass.
items.remaining: A linked fileUrl is still accepted from the body without a storage-host allow-list.

items.explanation: The person who last edited or submitted an exit interview, not only its creator, cannot review it (403). Existing review tests pass.
items.remaining: No submitter column exists; the last editor stands in for the submitter.

items.explanation: Documents and transcripts can no longer be attached to an interview that is reviewed, published or archived (409), so what the reviewer approved is what is published.

The message log, campaign stats, preference, list subscriptions and consent record are written on the one transaction handed to the callback (they used the shared connection, so there was no transaction at all). The unit-test mocks were adapted to pass the mock db as the transaction and to include the newsletter tables, and the real-SQL pglite test now creates those tables and still passes (disclosed).
items.remaining: The public GET still changes state; it is guarded by a signed, action-bound token.

items.explanation: A campaign-link unsubscribe also marks the recipient subscriptions to the distribution lists of that organization unsubscribed, in the same transaction. Proven on real SQL (pglite) not to fail; contract test pins the update.

batches.family: F12: publication needs a second person, and registration follows the session window and capacity

items.explanation: Moving an item from review to published is refused for the person who last changed it (who moved it to review), and republishing no longer rewrites the first publication time (coalesce). Existing status route tests pass.
items.remaining: The row records only its last editor, not a separate submitter; a submitted_by column is the proper fix.

items.explanation: Registration is refused (409) for a session that is not scheduled, outside its registration window, or at its maximum enrollment (counted from registered rows). The session-belongs-to-course and duplicate checks already existed. The route test mock gained the count helper and new cases for closed, not-yet-open, cancelled and full sessions (disclosed).
items.remaining: The capacity count is read then written, so two simultaneous registrations for the last place can both pass; a transactional lock or counter is still needed.

batches.family: Schema closure: the columns and indexes that let earlier partial fixes record the real fact instead of approximating it

items.explanation: Migration 0038 adds kpi_configurations.direction (higher_is_better or lower_is_better, null for rows that predate it). A target can be created with a direction, and the summary lets a stored direction decide; only a target with none keeps the threshold-order inference. Proven on PGlite (check constraint) and by unit tests.

Migration 0038 adds a partial unique index so an employer has at most one active primary contact; it refuses to apply over an employer that already has two. The create keeps its in-transaction demotion and answers a lost race with 409. Proven on PGlite, including the refusal over existing duplicates.

Migration 0038 adds committee_meetings.minutes_recorded_by and a check that the approver is not the recorder. Recording the minutes stores the recorder and approval refuses that person (403); a meeting recorded before the column existed falls back to its last editor.

Migration 0038 adds exit_interviews.submitted_by and a check that the reviewer is not the submitter. Submitting stores the submitter and review refuses that person (403), with the last-editor fallback only for earlier rows. Existing review tests pass.

Migration 0038 adds cms_pages.submitted_by. Moving an item to review records who did it, and publication is refused for that person, with the last-editor fallback only for earlier rows. Existing status tests pass.

No schema change was needed: the tables already carry is_active. The shared CRUD factory gains archiveColumn, so DELETE archives the template (is_active false, audited) instead of removing it, and the collections list active templates only. The B53 retain-on-delete pin was replaced by an archive pin (disclosed).

DELETE of a distribution list now archives it (is_active false), so the cascade that erased the subscribed, unsubscribed and unsubscribe-reason trail can no longer fire through the API; the collection lists active lists only.

Migration 0038 adds unique partial indexes (organization and SAML entity id; organization, OIDC issuer and client id), refusing to apply over duplicates; a duplicate create answers 409. The create now accepts requireGroups (at most 50 short names). Proven on PGlite.
items.remaining: No proof that the organization owns the identity domain: that needs a DNS or e-mail verification process with the identity provider, which a schema cannot supply.

batches.family: Database enforcement: constraints, triggers and columns that settle what application checks could only attempt

items.explanation: Migration 0040 adds new_engine to employer_execution_replay_mode, so an engine-change replay is stored as new_engine and not as a faithful exact re-run. Proven on PGlite; the requested mode still travels with the diff for idempotency.

Migration 0040 adds a unique index (organization, member, session) that refuses to apply over existing duplicates, and a BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE trigger that locks the session row and refuses a registration beyond max_enrollment (SQLSTATE 23514); a cancelled place frees a seat and a re-save of a registered row is not recounted. The CRUD factory gains mapCreateError so a lost race answers 409 (full, or already registered). Proven on PGlite.
Migration 0040 adds ml_predictions.subject_id. The case is verified against the organization (B08) and is now stored on the prediction row, and the audit entry and feedback carry it.

Migration 0040 adds ml_predictions.model_version, written by the prediction route. Feedback now defaults to the version the prediction recorded and refuses (409) a different one, so the version binding no longer depends on a column that was missing. The route test zod mock gained optional() on min() (disclosed).

The durable sent marker needed no new table: the warning is also the member's in-app notice, recorded in in_app_notifications under data.dedupeKey (unique per organization and member, migration 20261103) before the mail leaves; a second run, retry or overlap mails nothing more, and a failed send releases the record so the next run tries again. Proved on PostgreSQL (PGlite) for repeat, retry-after-failure and per-tier behaviour. The mocked notification-service test now mocks the marker (disclosed).
items.remaining: Nothing in the product sets an expiry or writes an expire entry yet, so the task still has nothing to warn about until an expiry policy is decided and implemented.

batches.family: Room booking: the booking store, its tenant isolation and the route that enforces the room's own rules

items.explanation: Platform 0041 evolves the room_bookings stub to its 26 missing declared columns, cache 0035 forces row-level security by organization, and the manifest reclassifies the table from LATENT_UNREACHABLE to TENANT_RLS_REQUIRED with SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE only. POST /api/meeting-rooms/[id]/bookings now accepts a booking only when evaluateBooking allows it (hours, blocked dates, duration, how far ahead, who may book, capacity, approval); a room needing approval holds the slot as scheduled until staff other than the booker confirm it. Proved against real SQL on PGlite, including the room-locking trigger. Not applied to a native database. The unused calendar-service placeholders (listMeetingRooms returned an empty list, checkRoomAvailability always answered available, bookMeetingRoom returned a generated id without storing anything, cancelRoomBooking reported success) were removed together with their four stub tests (disclosed); overlap is refused by a trigger that locks the room row (SQLSTATE 23P01, answered as 409).

The bookings path serves bookings (GET slots with details only for the caller's own bookings unless staff; POST; PATCH approve or decline; DELETE cancels and keeps the row), each scoped to the caller's organization, audited in the same transaction; a booking id of another organization or room is not found. The f12-b53 contract pin that listed this route as 501 was removed (disclosed).

batches.family: Code closure of partial fixes whose remaining part needed no external decision

items.explanation: getWalletSnapshot reads the latest balance, the page and the total inside one repeatable-read transaction, so they cannot disagree; the response also carries the total and hasMore is computed from it. Proved on PostgreSQL (PGlite) for paging, scoping to the member and organization, and an empty ledger. The route test mock now returns the snapshot (disclosed).

The six pension list reads take bounded limit (1..200, default 200 so existing callers are unchanged) and offset (0..1,000,000) through the shared listPage helper, so rows beyond the first page are reachable. The own-records route test mock and the B36 bounds pin were adapted to the offset call (disclosed).

A linked fileUrl must be a pointer into the organization's own document storage (verifiedLegacyBlobPath: configured storage account, document container, the organization's folder, no credential, no traversal) or the link is refused with 400. Tested with an own URL, another host, another organization's folder, a credential, a traversal and a metadata address.

Existing implementation, verified: the event update schema is strict and does not accept calendarId, so an update cannot re-point an event at another calendar; creation already checks the calendar belongs to the organization and is not another member's personal calendar. Pinned by a test.
